producer_report.summary: Each job's producer now runs in its own worktree (jobs/<id>/work) with its own build directory (jobs/<id>/target/produce). A new JobWorktree drop guard in state.rs clears both at producer start and removes both on every exit of produce_and_verify. The exits are a verdict, a stop, and an error; an error used to leave both behind. The disk bound of section 5 is added to disk.rs as in_flight_limit, Figures (T and S from the latest build-measurement record, else 6 GB and 0.2 GB), start_decision and Athena::start_hold. dispatch calls start_hold after the min_free_gb gate. A held start is the existing LowDisk hold: the job stays queued and a later drain starts it. max_in_flight = 1, or no other job in flight, is never held. The per-job worktree is the producer's isolated one-commit snapshot repository, not a linked `git worktree`, because a linked one would expose the user's history and records/ to the producer. CHANGELOG and the design note say this. Tests: unit tests in disk.rs and state.rs; go-level tests in drain.rs (per_job_worktree_* and in_flight_bound_*). With the guard disabled, the stale-start test and the error-escape test fail. Last runs: fmt check, clippy -D warnings and the policy scan pass. A full `cargo test --locked` before my last edit had one failure, in run/tests.rs. I removed the cause, and the run tests then passed. I did not rerun the whole suite after that.

criteria_check.criterion: A test through Athena::go (the real entry point) shows a job's producer runs in a fresh git worktree with its own target directory under the job's state directory, and that after the job ends both directories are gone, on success and on a failed or rejected job. Run: cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli.
criteria_check.evidence: Five tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (per_job_worktree_*) call Athena::go. A wrapper records the producer's workdir, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, whether .git exists, the target dir's entries and any stale file at the producer's start. Landed, rejected, failed, stale-start and error-escape cases assert: workdir == jobs/<id>/work with .git present; CARGO_TARGET_DIR == jobs/<id>/target/produce, empty or absent and a different path; no stale file seen; both directories gone after go returns. In the error case go returns Err. All five passed with `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- per_job_worktree in_flight_bound`, and again in the full suite. With the guard line commented out, the stale-start and error-escape tests failed. Deviation: the worktree is a fresh one-commit repository, not a linked `git worktree`; see open_issues.

They assert exact integers: 60 GB gives 7; two check slots give 6; a measured T 4 GB and S 1 GB give 9; the exact edge at 22.2 GB gives 1 and one byte less gives 0; below the reserve gives 0; the latest of two records wins in either order; the estimates are exactly 6_000_000_000 and 200_000_000. open_issues: Departure from the brief: it asks for a 'real git worktree', but the per-job worktree is the producer's isolated one-commit snapshot repository, not a linked `git worktree`. `git worktree list` will not show it. This follows the accepted plan. A linked worktree would give the producer the user's history and records/, and needs its own job. Does the user want that?

Departure from the reading: a bound of zero holds a start only while another job is in flight. A lone job is never held, because a held lone job could never start. min_free_gb still guards it. Please confirm.
The hold is reachable only when jobs overlap, which nothing does until build job 10. The tests make the other in-flight job by hand: a planted work dir plus a held job lock.

The in-flight check is a gate, not a lock. The probe takes a shared lock on another job's job.lock for microseconds, so a racing command on that job could be refused as already running, and two simultaneous starts can both pass. This is documented in the doc comments, CHANGELOG and design note.

The docs and doc comments do not define the 'free' figure precisely: it is free bytes now plus the bytes the other jobs' work and target/produce directories already use. The hold line shows both numbers.
mistakes: I first added a 'worktree' progress line in producer_snapshot. It broke an existing run/tests.rs test that counts progress lines. I removed it, so the plan's one ui line for work tree and target path is not in the code.
I named a test helper struct Watched, which clashed with an existing struct in drain.rs. I renamed it to OwnRun.
My first draft of a start_decision test asserted the wrong boundary (35 GB with 3 allowed fits 3, so it is not held). I corrected it to 30 GB before running it.
learnings: run/tests.rs has an existing test that counts the exact progress lines of a fake job. Any new ui.line in the run path breaks it, and the job may not edit that file.

The producer's CARGO_TARGET_DIR is jobs/<id>/target/produce, set by athena_agent::env. The fake driver applies a scenario's edits after the script returns, so a script sees the workdir before its edits.
flock-based job locks conflict between two open handles in one process. A test can hold try_lock_job and the production probe sees it as held.
drain.rs already has a struct named Watched, so new helpers there need other names.
test_config() ends with the [disk] table, so appending [drain.pipeline] works. `[drain.pipeline]` is accepted and left out of the reading digest.
